/etc/mpfree-test/ethernet-details.sh.text:
#!/bin/sh
# MPFree Ethernet details - STRICTLY READ-ONLY.
# Streamed over SSH stdin by collect-over-ssh.sh --ethernet (on the running
# stock system), and run by the kexec test build to record the same details on
# the USB stick, so the two can be compared line by line.
#
# Answers: was the Ethernet PHY found, and is the kernel holding it in reset;
# which clocks feed the Ethernet controller and are they running; how are the
# PHY's reset and interrupt pins set; and what did the kernel say about the
# controller, its MDIO bus and the PHY.
#
# It reads procfs, sysfs, debugfs (only if it is already mounted) and the
# kernel log, and asks ethtool (only if installed) for its query output. It
# never mounts, never changes an interface or a service, never writes a file or
# a register, and never prints a MAC address.
set -u
R="${MPFREE_FAKE_ROOT:-}"
printf 'MPFREE ETHERNET DETAILS - READ ONLY\n'
printf 'MAC addresses are replaced with <MAC>.\n'

section() { printf '\n=== %s ===\n' "$1"; }
redact() { sed -e 's/[0-9A-Fa-f][0-9A-Fa-f]\(:[0-9A-Fa-f][0-9A-Fa-f]\)\{5\}/<MAC>/g'; }
value() { [ -r "$1" ] && cat "$1" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1; return 0; }
show() { [ -r "$1" ] && printf '  %s: %s\n' "$2" "$(value "$1")"; return 0; }
link_name() { [ -L "$1" ] && basename "$(readlink "$1")"; return 0; }
# The tests run this against a fake tree, whose kernel log is a file in it.
kernel_log() { if [ -n "$R" ]; then cat "$R/kernel-log" 2>/dev/null; else dmesg 2>/dev/null; fi; }

section 'Kernel'
printf 'release: %s\n' "$(value "$R/proc/sys/kernel/osrelease")"
printf 'uptime: %s s\n' "$(cut -d' ' -f1 "$R/proc/uptime" 2>/dev/null)"

section 'Network interfaces (not lo)'
for d in "$R"/sys/class/net/*; do
  [ -d "$d" ] || continue
  name=${d##*/}
  [ "$name" = lo ] && continue
  printf '%s\n' "$name"
  show "$d/operstate" operstate
  show "$d/flags" flags
  show "$d/carrier" carrier
  show "$d/mtu" mtu
  printf '  driver: %s\n' "$(link_name "$d/device/driver")"
  if [ -L "$d/phydev" ]; then
    printf '  phy: %s\n' "$(link_name "$d/phydev")"
    show "$d/phydev/phy_id" '  phy_id'
    show "$d/phydev/phy_interface" '  phy_interface'
    printf '    phy driver: %s\n' "$(link_name "$d/phydev/driver")"
  else
    printf '  phy: none attached\n'
  fi
done

section 'MDIO buses'
for b in "$R"/sys/class/mdio_bus/*; do
  [ -d "$b" ] || continue
  printf '%s\n' "${b##*/}"
  for f in transfers errors reads writes transfers_1 errors_1 reads_1 writes_1; do
    show "$b/statistics/$f" "$f"
  done
done

section 'MDIO devices'
for m in "$R"/sys/bus/mdio_bus/devices/*; do
  [ -d "$m" ] || continue
  printf '%s\n' "${m##*/}"
  show "$m/phy_id" phy_id
  show "$m/phy_interface" phy_interface
  show "$m/phy_has_fixups" phy_has_fixups
  printf '  driver: %s\n' "$(link_name "$m/driver")"
  printf '  attached to: %s\n' "$(link_name "$m/attached_dev")"
done

section 'Interrupts of the Ethernet controller and PHY'
grep -i -E 'eth[0-9]|end[0-9]|stmmac|mdio|ff290000|macirq' "$R/proc/interrupts" 2>/dev/null || printf '(none listed)\n'

section 'PHY supply (VCCIO_PMU) and other Ethernet regulators'
for r in "$R"/sys/class/regulator/regulator.*; do
  [ -r "$r/name" ] || continue
  rname=$(value "$r/name")
  case "$rname" in
    VCCIO_PMU|*[Gg][Mm][Aa][Cc]*|*[Ll][Aa][Nn]*|*[Pp][Hh][Yy]*)
      printf '%s (%s)\n' "$rname" "${r##*/}"
      show "$r/state" state
      show "$r/microvolts" microvolts
      show "$r/num_users" num_users
      ;;
  esac
done

section 'debugfs'
if grep -q ' /sys/kernel/debug debugfs ' "$R/proc/mounts" 2>/dev/null; then
  printf 'mounted at /sys/kernel/debug\n'

  section 'GPIO lines in use (debugfs gpio; the PHY reset is gpio4 B0, its interrupt gpio3 B7)'
  cat "$R/sys/kernel/debug/gpio" 2>/dev/null || printf '(unreadable)\n'

  section 'Clocks of the Ethernet controller (debugfs clk_summary)'
  if [ -r "$R/sys/kernel/debug/clk/clk_summary" ]; then
    head -n 3 "$R/sys/kernel/debug/clk/clk_summary"
    grep -E 'mac|gmac|_peri' "$R/sys/kernel/debug/clk/clk_summary"
  else
    printf '(unreadable)\n'
  fi

  section 'Ethernet pins (debugfs pinctrl)'
  for p in "$R"/sys/kernel/debug/pinctrl/*; do
    [ -r "$p/pinmux-pins" ] || continue
    printf '%s pinmux-pins:\n' "${p##*/}"
    grep -E 'ff290000|\(gpio4-8\)|\(gpio3-15\)' "$p/pinmux-pins" 2>/dev/null
    if [ -r "$p/pinconf-pins" ]; then
      printf '%s pinconf-pins:\n' "${p##*/}"
      grep -E '\(gpio4-8\)|\(gpio3-15\)' "$p/pinconf-pins" 2>/dev/null
    fi
  done

  section 'Devices waiting for a driver (debugfs devices_deferred)'
  cat "$R/sys/kernel/debug/devices_deferred" 2>/dev/null || printf '(unreadable)\n'
else
  printf 'debugfs is not mounted; this script does not mount it\n'
fi

section 'Kernel messages about the Ethernet controller, MDIO bus and PHY'
kernel_log | grep -i -E 'ff290000|stmmac|dwmac|mdio|rtl82|eth0|end0' | redact

section 'ethtool (queries only)'
if command -v ethtool >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  for d in "$R"/sys/class/net/*; do
    name=${d##*/}
    [ "$name" = lo ] && continue
    [ -d "$d" ] || continue
    printf -- '--- ethtool -i %s ---\n' "$name"
    ethtool -i "$name" 2>&1 | redact
    printf -- '--- ethtool %s ---\n' "$name"
    ethtool "$name" 2>&1 | redact
  done
else
  printf 'ethtool is not installed\n'
fi
printf '\nEND OF ETHERNET DETAILS\n'

/etc/mpfree-test/ethernet-retry.sh.text:
#!/bin/sh
# MPFree kexec test boot: record the Ethernet details; start eth0 again if it failed to start.
out=/run/mpfree-test-eth
mkdir -p "$out"
say() { echo "mpfree-test-ethernet: $*"; }
grep -q ' /sys/kernel/debug debugfs ' /proc/mounts || mount -t debugfs debugfs /sys/kernel/debug
uptime_s() { cut -d. -f1 /proc/uptime; }
wait_until() { while [ "$(uptime_s)" -lt "$1" ]; do sleep 1; done; }
details() { sh /etc/mpfree-test/ethernet-details.sh > "$out/ethernet-$1.txt" 2>&1; say "recorded ethernet-$1.txt"; }
eth0_up() { f=$(cat /sys/class/net/eth0/flags 2>/dev/null) || return 1; [ $((f & 1)) = 1 ]; }
details "1-early-$(uptime_s)s"
wait_until 15
details 2-at-15s
n=3
for at in 20 45 90; do
  wait_until "$at"
  if eth0_up; then
    say "eth0 is up at $at s (operstate $(cat /sys/class/net/eth0/operstate)); no retry needed"
    details "$n-at-${at}s-eth0-up"
    exit 0
  fi
  say "eth0 is not up at $at s; starting it again"
  ip link set eth0 up 2>&1 | sed 's/^/mpfree-test-ethernet: ip: /'
  sleep 3
  details "$n-at-${at}s-after-retry"
  n=$((n + 1))
done
say "eth0 retries done"

/etc/mpfree-test/internal-off.sh.text:
R=''
# MPFree: switch the MPC's internal eMMC and SD card off, before anything can touch them.
# (The R='' line is an empty root prefix; only tests change it.)
# Run first thing at boot (mpfree-test-internal-off.service, before udev and every mount). After MPFree's
# soft-reboot hook, this system runs on Akai's kernel with Akai's device tree, where both controllers are on;
# after a kexec jump they are already hidden and there is nothing to do. It
#   1. waits up to 10 s for the old system's writable filesystems on the eMMC to be let go (the soft-reboot
#      detaches Akai's /data; systemd synced it first). Akai's root is read-only (dm-verity), not waited for;
#   2. marks every eMMC and SD block device read-only;
#   3. unbinds the two controllers' driver (the eMMC's at ff0f0000, the SD card's at ff0c0000), so the
#      kernel removes their block devices; nothing is written to them, before or after;
#   4. checks that no eMMC or SD block device is left, and removes stale /dev/disk links to them.
# If any step fails it keeps its notes and the kernel log on the stick's own log partition (partition 2,
# "mpfree-test-log", MPFree's; never anything of the MPC's), exits 1, and the unit's FailureAction powers the
# MPC off: MPFree never runs with the internal storage reachable. Taking the stick out gives Akai's system at
# the next power-on. Otherwise it writes only /run (RAM), /dev links (RAM), the controllers' sysfs unbind
# files and the kernel log.
[ -n "$R" ] || PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
HOSTS="ff0f0000 ff0c0000"
say() { echo "mpfree-internal-off: $*" > "$R/dev/kmsg" 2>/dev/null; echo "mpfree-internal-off: $*" >> "$R/run/mpfree-internal-off.txt"; }
stop() {
  say "STOP: $1; powering off"
  log=''
  for u in "$R"/sys/class/block/sd*/uevent; do
    grep -qx 'PARTNAME=mpfree-test-log' "$u" 2>/dev/null || continue
    p=${u%/uevent}
    case "$(readlink -f "$p")" in */usb*) log=${p##*/} ;; esac
  done
  m="$R/run/mpfree-internal-off-log"
  if [ -n "$log" ] && [ -b "$R/dev/$log" ] && mkdir -p "$m" &&
      mount -t ext4 -o rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,sync "$R/dev/$log" "$m"; then
    d="$m/boot-$(cat "$R/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id")"
    mkdir -p "$d" && { cat "$R/run/mpfree-internal-off.txt"; dmesg; } > "$d/internal-off.txt" 2>&1
    umount "$m"
  fi
  exit 1
}
how=kexec
[ -e "$R/run/mpfree-hook/soft-reboot" ] && how=soft-reboot
say "started at $(cut -d' ' -f1 "$R/proc/uptime") s (after $how)"
held() {   # prints a writable filesystem still mounted from the eMMC or SD card, even a detached one
  for f in "$R"/sys/fs/ext4/* "$R"/sys/fs/f2fs/*; do
    [ -e "$f" ] || continue
    n=${f##*/}
    case "$n" in
      mmcblk*) echo "$n"; return 0 ;;
      dm-*) for s in "$R"/sys/block/"$n"/slaves/*; do
              case "${s##*/}" in mmcblk*) [ "$(cat "$R/sys/block/$n/ro" 2>/dev/null)" = 1 ] || { echo "$n"; return 0; } ;; esac
            done ;;
    esac
  done
  return 1
}
n=0
while busy=$(held); do
  [ "$n" -ge 10 ] && { sync; stop "$busy is still mounted after 10 s"; }
  sleep 1; n=$((n + 1))
done
if command -v blockdev > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  for b in "$R"/sys/block/mmcblk*; do
    [ -e "$b" ] || continue
    for d in "$R/dev/${b##*/}" "$R/dev/${b##*/}"p*; do
      [ -b "$d" ] && blockdev --setro "$d" 2>/dev/null
    done
  done
fi
for a in $HOSTS; do
  for dev in "$R"/sys/bus/platform/devices/"$a".*; do
    [ -e "$dev/driver" ] || continue
    name=${dev##*/}
    echo "$name" > "$dev/driver/unbind" || stop "could not unbind $name"
    say "switched off $name"
  done
done
left() {   # prints a controller still bound, or an eMMC or SD block device still there
  for a in $HOSTS; do
    for dev in "$R"/sys/bus/platform/devices/"$a".*; do
      [ -e "$dev/driver" ] && { echo "${dev##*/} still has its driver"; return 0; }
    done
  done
  for b in "$R"/sys/block/mmcblk*; do
    [ -e "$b" ] && { echo "${b##*/} is still there"; return 0; }
  done
  return 1
}
n=0
while what=$(left); do   # the kernel removes them as it unbinds; allow it a moment
  [ "$n" -ge 5 ] && stop "$what"
  sleep 1; n=$((n + 1))
done
for l in "$R"/dev/disk/by-*/*; do
  case "$(readlink "$l" 2>/dev/null)" in *mmcblk*) rm -f "$l" ;; esac
done
say "done at $(cut -d' ' -f1 "$R/proc/uptime") s: no eMMC or SD card block device is left"

/etc/mpfree-test/power.sh.text:
#!/bin/sh
# MPFree test boot: shut down or restart, as the pad player's power card asked (one word in /run/mpfree-app/power-request).
# Only `poweroff` and `restart` are acted on. The file is in the pad player's own folder, so it is never
# followed if it is a link, and its content is never printed.
f=/run/mpfree-app/power-request
[ -e "$f" ] || [ -L "$f" ] || exit 0
word=
if [ -f "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ]; then
  IFS= read -r word < "$f" || :
fi
rm -f "$f"
case "$word" in
  poweroff) target=poweroff.target ;;
  restart) target=reboot.target ;;
  *)
    echo "mpfree-test-power: ignored a request that was not poweroff or restart" > /dev/kmsg
    exit 0
    ;;
esac
echo "mpfree-test-power: the pad player asked for $word" > /dev/kmsg
# A note on the stick's log partition, where the log service keeps this boot's logs, so the next boot can
# show how this one ended. Nothing else is written.
d=/run/mpfree-log/boot-$(cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id 2>/dev/null)
if [ -d "$d" ]; then
  { echo "asked: $word"; cat /proc/uptime; } > "$d/power.txt" 2>&1
  journalctl -b --no-pager -o short-monotonic > "$d/journal.txt" 2>&1
fi
sync
exec systemctl --no-block --job-mode=replace-irreversibly start "$target"

/etc/mpfree-test/save-logs.sh.text:
#!/bin/sh
# MPFree kexec test boot: copy logs to the stick's log partition (and nothing else).
dev=/dev/disk/by-partuuid/@LOG_UUID@
i=0
while [ ! -e "$dev" ] && [ "$i" -lt 60 ]; do sleep 1; i=$((i + 1)); done
[ -e "$dev" ] || { echo "mpfree-test: log partition not found" > /dev/kmsg; exit 1; }
mkdir -p /run/mpfree-log
mount -t ext4 -o rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,sync "$dev" /run/mpfree-log || exit 1
d=/run/mpfree-log/boot-$(cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id)
mkdir -p "$d"
while :; do
  dmesg > "$d/dmesg.txt" 2>&1
  journalctl -b --no-pager -o short-monotonic > "$d/journal.txt" 2>&1
  systemctl --failed --no-pager > "$d/failed-units.txt" 2>&1
  systemctl list-units --no-pager > "$d/units.txt" 2>&1
  { ip addr; ip route; } > "$d/network.txt" 2>&1
  cat /proc/cmdline > "$d/cmdline.txt" 2>&1
  cp /run/mpfree-test-eth/*.txt "$d/" 2>/dev/null
  cp /run/mpfree-app/report.txt "$d/" 2>/dev/null
  sync
  sleep 10
done

/etc/mpfree-test/start-app.sh.text:
#!/bin/sh
# MPFree test boot (--app-user): start the pad player, as the mpfree user. mpfree-test-storage.service
# mounted its drum kits (partition 3, read-only) and its saved settings and files (partition 4) as root.
# This script changes nothing.
if grep -q ' /run/mpfree-data ' /proc/mounts; then
  exec /etc/mpfree-test/mpfree app --kits /run/mpfree-kits/kits.bin --keep-screen --data /run/mpfree-data --power-request /run/mpfree-app/power-request
fi
echo "mpfree-test-app: the data partition is not mounted, so nothing is saved"
exec /etc/mpfree-test/mpfree app --kits /run/mpfree-kits/kits.bin --keep-screen --power-request /run/mpfree-app/power-request

/etc/mpfree-test/storage.sh.text:
#!/bin/sh
# MPFree test boot (--app-user): get the pad player's storage ready, as root, before it starts as the
# mpfree user (uid 960). Its drum kits are on the stick's partition 3, mounted read-only. Partition 4 holds
# its saved settings and files, mounted read-write; files there that are not yet the mpfree user's are given
# to it (find -xdev stays on partition 4), except the eMMC backups in backup/, which stay root's (the pad player
# only reads them, through its group). This runs before the pad player starts and not again when it
# restarts, so no process of the mpfree user can change those folders while they are walked.
# The framebuffer's sysfs `pan` file is opened to the mpfree group (in RAM, until power-off), so the pad
# player can ask the kernel to show the screen.
# It writes nothing else and never fails the boot: a step that does not work is noted in the kernel log,
# and the pad player starts without it, as it did when start-app.sh did this.
dev=/dev/disk/by-partuuid/@KITS_UUID@
i=0
while [ ! -e "$dev" ] && [ "$i" -lt 30 ]; do sleep 1; i=$((i + 1)); done
mkdir -p /run/mpfree-kits
if ! grep -q ' /run/mpfree-kits ' /proc/mounts; then
  mount -t ext4 -o ro,nosuid,nodev,noexec "$dev" /run/mpfree-kits ||
    echo "mpfree-test-storage: the kit partition did not mount" > /dev/kmsg
fi
data=/dev/disk/by-partuuid/@DATA_UUID@
i=0
while [ ! -e "$data" ] && [ "$i" -lt 5 ]; do sleep 1; i=$((i + 1)); done
mkdir -p /run/mpfree-data
if grep -q ' /run/mpfree-data ' /proc/mounts ||
    mount -t ext4 -o rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,noatime "$data" /run/mpfree-data; then
  mkdir -p /run/mpfree-data/files/plugins
  find /run/mpfree-data -xdev -path /run/mpfree-data/backup -prune -o ! -user 960 -exec chown -h 960:960 {} \; ||
    echo "mpfree-test-storage: some files on partition 4 could not be given to mpfree" > /dev/kmsg
  # Plugins in files/plugins are libraries the pad player loads, and a library can't be loaded from a noexec
  # mount. So only that folder allows it: a bind of it over itself, remounted exec (still nosuid and nodev).
  # The rest of partition 4 stays noexec.
  p=/run/mpfree-data/files/plugins
  if ! grep -q " $p " /proc/mounts; then
    { mount --bind "$p" "$p" && mount -o remount,bind,exec,nosuid,nodev "$p"; } ||
      echo "mpfree-test-storage: files/plugins could not be made loadable, so plugins there will not start" > /dev/kmsg
  fi
  # Partition 4 fills the stick but its filesystem may be smaller: grow it to fill the partition, online
  # (the kernel does it while mounted, and writes only partition 4). When it already fills it, nothing changes.
  if [ -x /usr/sbin/resize2fs ]; then
    ( /usr/sbin/resize2fs "$data" > /run/mpfree-data-grow.txt 2>&1 ||
        echo "mpfree-test-storage: partition 4's filesystem did not grow; see /run/mpfree-data-grow.txt" > /dev/kmsg ) &
  fi
else
  echo "mpfree-test-storage: the data partition did not mount, so nothing is saved" > /dev/kmsg
fi
for p in /sys/class/graphics/fb*/pan; do
  [ -e "$p" ] || continue
  chgrp 960 "$p" && chmod g+w "$p" ||
    echo "mpfree-test-storage: could not open $p to mpfree" > /dev/kmsg
done
exit 0

DefaultDependencies=no
Wants=mpfree-test-storage.service

Before=shutdown.target
IgnoreOnIsolate=yes

StartLimitIntervalSec=60

[Service]
Type=simple

Group=mpfree
ExecStart=/bin/sh /etc/mpfree-test/start-app.sh
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=2
LimitRTPRIO=70
LimitMEMLOCK=infinity
NoNewPrivileges=yes
CapabilityBoundingSet=
AmbientCapabilities=
RuntimeDirectory=mpfree-app
RuntimeDirectoryPreserve=yes

[Install]
WantedBy=sysinit.target

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/bin/sh -c 'journalctl -b -f -n 100 --no-pager --no-hostname -o short-monotonic 2>&1 | /etc/mpfree-test/mpfree-screen-log --rotation @ROTATION@'
Restart=always
RestartSec=5
Nice=10

[Install]
WantedBy=sysinit.target

/etc/systemd/system/mpfree-test-splash.s.text:
[Unit]
Description=MPFree test boot: startup screen before the live log
DefaultDependencies=no
Conflicts=shutdown.target
Before=shutdown.target mpfree-test-screen.service
IgnoreOnIsolate=yes

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
ExecStart=/etc/mpfree-test/mpfree-splash --framebuffer --rotation @ROTATION@ --seconds 6
TimeoutStartSec=20

[Install]
WantedBy=sysinit.target

/etc/systemd/system/mpfree-test-sshd.ser.text:
[Unit]
Description=MPFree test boot: key-only root SSH on port 2222
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
RuntimeDirectory=sshd
RuntimeDirectoryMode=0755
ExecStartPre=/usr/sbin/sshd -t -f /etc/mpfree-test/sshd_config
ExecStart=/usr/sbin/sshd -D -e -f /etc/mpfree-test/sshd_config
Restart=always
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

/etc/systemd/system/mpfree-test-storage..text:
[Unit]
Description=MPFree test boot: mount the pad player's kits and saved files, as root, before it starts
DefaultDependencies=no
After=systemd-journald.service systemd-udevd.service mpfree-test-internal-off.service
Conflicts=shutdown.target
Before=shutdown.target
IgnoreOnIsolate=yes

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
ExecStart=/bin/sh /etc/mpfree-test/storage.sh
TimeoutStartSec=90

/etc/udev/rules.d/00-mpfree-internal-off.text:
# MPFree: the MPC's internal eMMC and SD card are not MPFree's. mpfree-test-internal-off.service removes
# them before udev starts; should one appear anyway, systemd and udisks leave it alone.
SUBSYSTEM=="block", KERNEL=="mmcblk*", ENV{SYSTEMD_READY}="0", ENV{UDISKS_IGNORE}="1", ENV{UDISKS_AUTO}="0"

stub:
#!/bin/sh
# MPFree kexec test boot: this program is disabled on the test stick.
echo "mpfree-test: blocked $0 $*" > /dev/kmsg 2>/dev/null
echo "mpfree-test: $0 is disabled on this test boot" >&2
exit 1
